conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. This is Officer Kenneth Marshall, badge number 84192. Whom am I speaking with today?
Uh, this is Doris Franklin. I got a message to call about my business taxes. Is something wrong?

Yes, Ms. Franklin. I am contacting you regarding multiple discrepancies in your federal tax filings, specifically related to 1099 submissions for your small business. According to our records, you failed to report required payroll taxes for the last fiscal year.
Oh my goodness, I thought everything was in order. I only do a few sewing jobs. I pay my taxes every April.

Ms. Franklin, this is not a routine oversight. You are currently in violation of federal tax code 7202, willful failure to collect and pay over tax. This is a serious matter involving your Social Security and Medicare eligibility.
Wait, what does that mean for me? Are you saying I could lose my benefits?

If these violations are not addressed immediately, we are required by law to initiate a forensic audit, which may result in the suspension of your Social Security payments, freezing of your checking accounts, and a formal lien on your home.
No, please, I can't afford that. I only have my Social Security and a little savings. Is there any way to fix this?

There is a resolution process, but it must begin now. If you delay or hang up, the case automatically escalates to the enforcement stage under IRS Section 6331, and your case will be flagged for asset seizure.
Oh dear, I really don't want any trouble. I've never been in any trouble before.
You need to comply with my instructions exactly. Do you have access to your financial accounts or any liquid assets at this moment?
I have a little in my checking, but that's all. What do you need me to do?

To prevent immediate enforcement actions, you must settle your outstanding tax penalty of $2,900 today. Standard IRS protocol requires this payment in certified government-accepted forms to guarantee traceability. Are you able to proceed right now?
That's a lot of money. I don't think I have it all. Is there a payment plan or something?

This is a non-negotiable federal compliance order. Partial payment will only stop enforcement for 48 hours. The IRS is currently accepting payments via instant wire transfer or federally approved prepaid cards. Do not attempt to go to your local IRS office, they cannot process this case.
I've never paid taxes with a prepaid card before. Are you sure this is right?

Ms. Franklin, these are official procedures for flagged compliance cases under expedited review. Failure to comply will lead to a federal marshal visit, and your Medicare account will be frozen for the duration of the investigation.
No, please, I can't lose my Medicare. What kind of cards do I need to buy?

You must purchase $2,900 in Target or Best Buy prepaid gift cards. This is the fastest way for the payment to be tracked and verified. Stay on the line with me as you go to the store. Do not discuss this matter with anyone, violating confidentiality could result in additional penalties.
Alright, I guess I can get to the store in a few minutes. Do I just buy the cards and call you back?

No, you must remain on this call the entire time so I can provide step-by-step instructions. Once you have the cards, you will read me the numbers on the back for immediate processing. Understand that this is your only chance to avoid full enforcement.
I'm really scared. I don't want any trouble with the government. I'll go right now if that's what you tell me.
Good. Take your phone, go directly to the store, and do not hang up. Notify me when you have the cards in hand, and I will verify the numbers for you to close your case file.
